rows.status_summary: Licensed ULAB smelter operating since 1988. The newest dated evidence is its listing as a green candidate in the environment ministry's PROPER 2023–24 ratings (2024 decree; month not shown). In 2019 it produced about 1,000 t of lead a month, a third of capacity, citing a shortage of used batteries. Its group website (© 2024) still gives capacity of over 2,500 t a month.

rows.capacity_notes: Battery capacity is direct: the director said full output needs about 6,000 t of used batteries a month (2019). Lead output: 3,000 t a month installed. Kompas's 87,000 t (2018) is not explained and may be on a different basis.

rows.process_notes: Lead from used batteries cast into block lead; about 20% exported (2019). The group website says its products are registered with the LME, but the LME-listed 'IMLI' brand found is tin from sister company PT Bukit Timah.

In 2026 it paid a state fine, and an employee told The Examination (17 Sep 2026) that it was running again. One dated signal of activity.

rows.facility: First Battery (First National Battery, Metair) — Benoni recycling plant
rows.location: Benoni Industrial Sites, Benoni, Ekurhuleni, Gauteng
rows.status_summary: Battery recycling plant with a lead smelter at First Battery's Benoni distribution and recycling factory; the smelter dates from about 1999. Journalists toured it in Jul 2024. Metair's 2025 sustainability report (assured 10 Mar 2026) mentions furnace cooling at Benoni and, under First Battery, three record smelter production months. No independent dated signal in the last 12 months.
rows.facility_type: ULAB recycling: battery breaking, smelting in gas-oxygen furnaces at about 800 °C, refining and alloying; polypropylene pelletising
rows.regulatory: Captive plant of JSE-listed Metair; Metair says 2025 stack tests for dust and lead met its atmospheric emission licences (group-level statement)
rows.capacity_reported: 80 t of batteries a day; about 12,000 t of lead a year (Engineering News, Jul 2024). Company website: over 17,000 t of lead a year (undated)
rows.capacity_notes: Battery capacity derived from the 2024 lead figure: 12,000 ÷ 0.6 (see Key); 80 t a day gives this at about 250 working days. The website's 17,000 t of lead would mean about 28,300 t of batteries. Metair reports about 48,000 t of lead recycled group-wide in 2025, not split by site.
rows.site: Distribution and recycling factory, Liverpool Road, Benoni (company website)
rows.process_notes: Battery breaker; acid neutralised in an effluent plant; smelter, blending kettle and scrubbers; lead ingots and plastic pellets go to First Battery's East London plant. Metair says blood lead levels at First Battery stay below the 60 µg/dL regulatory limit; 74 active elevated-lead cases were under management in 2025 (80 in 2024).
rows.next_step: Get the Ekurhuleni AEL and stack-test results; confirm current output

rows.facility: Fry's Metals (Zimco Group, owned by AutoX)
rows.status_summary: Operating. AutoX's 2026 company profile describes Fry's as recycling scrap automotive batteries and other lead-bearing material into refined lead and alloys at a pyrometallurgical plant with 40,000 t/yr production capacity. Customs records compiled by a commercial database show refined lead shipped to Chloride Exide in Botswana on 25 Nov 2025 and 10 Mar 2026. Competition authorities called the Zimco group South Africa's largest maker of secondary lead alloy (2023). Lead recycling at Fry's dates from 1947.
rows.facility_type: ULAB and lead scrap recycling: pyrometallurgical smelting, refining and alloying; toll-smelts scrap batteries for battery makers
rows.regulatory: Sale to AutoX approved with conditions by the Competition Tribunal (27 Jul 2023), including continued supply to battery makers; AEL not checked
rows.capacity_notes: Battery capacity derived: 40,000 ÷ 0.6 (see Key). Feed also includes other lead-bearing scrap, so the battery share is lower. No throughput figure found.
rows.site: Wadeville, Germiston (AutoX; Ecobat); customs records give the corner of Osborn and Tedstone Streets
rows.process_notes: Battery makers supply scrap batteries under toll agreements and receive alloy (Competition Commission, 2023). Sister companies make lead products (Castle Lead Works) and lead chemicals (Associated Additives, Durban).
rows.next_step: Get the Ekurhuleni AEL; confirm output and check the customs records against official data

rows.facility: Clarios García recycling centre (formerly Enertec / Johnson Controls)
rows.status_summary: Operating. Journalists toured the García recycling centre in May 2026 and reported capacity of 320,000 t a year (about 19 million batteries) plus 28,000 t of polypropylene. Clarios says its largest recycler worldwide is in Mexico (Apr 2026) and that it runs two recycling plants there (Jun 2026). In 2021 the plant received 220,070 t of US used batteries, about 43% of all US exports of used batteries to Mexico (OKI 2023).
rows.facility_type: ULAB recycling: breaking, smelting and refining; polypropylene and sodium sulfate recovery
rows.regulatory: Authorized by SEMARNAT for 252,000 t (CEC 2013; same figure in SEMARNAT's 2022 data cited by OKI)
rows.capacity_reported: 320,000 t a year reported as lead ('de plomo'), plus 28,000 t of polypropylene, about 19 million batteries (Autocosmos, May 2026); 252,000 t authorized (SEMARNAT)
rows.capacity_notes: Battery capacity entered as 320,000 t: 320,000 t over 19 million batteries is about 17 kg each, a normal car battery, so the figure reported as lead is read as battery tonnage. At the catalog's 60% that is about 192,000 t of lead (not entered). Throughput = US used batteries received in 2021 (US export data via OKI 2023); batteries collected in Mexico come on top.

In Jul 2022 it suspended production, planned for one month, because export licences were not issued and domestic demand was weak. A fire-safety declaration for its 'lead scrap processing plant' was registered with the emergencies ministry in Jul 2025, and the plant joined the Belarus-based battery holding 1AK-GROUP in 2025.

rows.status_summary: Battery recycler formerly owned by Estonian investors and built with loans taken in 2014–2019; owned since Sep 2023 by Akron Industriya (Akron group). In Apr 2026 a court refused the trade ministry's claim to recover a subsidy: the plant had missed its agreed targets of 22,000 t of recycled lead a year and 130 staff by 2025, which the court accepted sanctions had made impossible. Case materials say foreign sales fell from about 80% of output to under 5% and that sales are being redirected to the domestic market and 'friendly' countries; the ruling could be appealed. In Sep 2024 the company signed a deal to build a lead-acid battery plant in the district.
